title: The winter cold tongue and slope current off southern Vietnam
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

paper.title: A gap in the Indo‐Pacific warm pool over the South China Sea in boreal winter: Seasonal development and interannual variability

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: In boreal winter a cold tongue off southern Vietnam keeps South China Sea surface temperature well below that of the surrounding waters (a gap in the warm pool).
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'a conspicuous gap over the South China Sea where SST is considerably lower than over the oceans both to the west and east'; 'a distinct cold tongue in the winter SST climatology'.
criteria.how_to_test: December-February mean SST map 2011-2020; cold-tongue minimum minus waters at the same latitudes east of the Philippines or in the Sulu Sea where inside the domain (otherwise relative to the basin east of 112 E); position of the cold-tongue axis.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: temperature contrast +/-0.5 C; cold-tongue axis within 1 degree)

criteria.title: Finding 2
criteria.claim: An intense southward slope current south of Vietnam, exceeding 0.5 m/s, is the western boundary current of the winter cyclonic gyre and forms the cold tongue by cold advection.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'This slope current exceeds 0.5 m s-1 in speed and advects cold water from the north. This cold advection results in a distinct cold tongue'.
criteria.how_to_test: Monthly climatology of the maximum southward speed along the slope off southern Vietnam (about 10-13 N); horizontal advection's share of the November-February cooling of the cold-tongue box from the evaluator-only CMOMS heat budget (X_HEAT).
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: peak speed +/-0.1 m/s; sign and rank of horizontal advection exact)

criteria.title: Finding 4
criteria.claim: The cold tongue's interannual variability follows ENSO: during El Nino the monsoon weakens, the circulation spins down and the cold tongue warms.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: variability 'highly correlated with eastern equatorial Pacific SST'; 'In an El Nino the winter monsoon weakens, causing the SCS ocean circulation to spin down'.
criteria.how_to_test: Testable: cold-tongue SST and slope-current anomalies in the 2015/16 El Nino winter versus La Nina winters (event years from published classifications). Not testable: the monsoon weakening (no winds) and a robust correlation with Pacific SST (no index; ten winters).
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: anomaly signs exact for the 2015/16 winter)

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: Cold-tongue index (winter SST relative to surrounding waters); slope-current speed along the shelf break off southern Vietnam; the winter months used; a heat-advection estimate (advection terms from the velocity and temperature) or a stated proxy.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: Model fields versus the paper's satellite data; ten winters with few ENSO events; no ENSO index or winds supplied.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
